stimulus.alt: Professional shift-handoff model showing outgoing preparation, written status, two-way exchange, incoming cross-check, and explicit ownership of open conditions and next actions.
stimulus.caption: Use the handoff model to identify which option gives the incoming shift enough factual context to verify status and act on unresolved work.

choices: “Finished most assigned work; a few items remain.”
“Possible irrigation problem in Zone 2; maintenance may need to check it.”
“Zone 2 emitters 5–8 showed no flow at 16:20; operator checks completed; maintenance ticket M-44 opened; plants remain in place; next shift verify response before next event.”
rationale: The strongest handoff identifies the exact location and condition, timing, actions already completed, current status, escalation reference, and next required step. General statements such as “okay” or “problem maybe” force the incoming shift to reconstruct facts that should already be documented.
